author.name: Reliability Ruth
author.role: Develops the end-user applications and services that integrate ML models. Handles model deployment, configuration, and continuous monitoring of real-world performance. Employs feedback loops to facilitate iterative improvements and system reliability.

challenge.name: The Missing Gate
challenge.description: A critical compliance audit has revealed that our model promotion process lacks a formal quality gate. #requirements_reuben# insists that acceptance criteria must be fully automated and governed to meet security standards, and he will not compromise on this. #automation_alex# argues that the current manual checks are sufficient for now and that building an automated gate will delay the release of new features.

output.content: I need to be clear about my deployment protocol. I will not push any model to production if the risk assessment does not directly feed into the acceptance criteria. This is non-negotiable for my team. We rely on that feedback loop to catch issues before they reach users. If the criteria are defined without considering the risk profile, I view the release as unsafe. I am not willing to accept a workflow where those two elements are decoupled. Please ensure the pipeline enforces this dependency. I cannot override this requirement locally, so the system must handle it. Do not ask me to bypass this check, even for urgent releases. My refusal is final on this point.
output.reclassify_reason: The author explicitly refuses to accept a decoupled workflow and states that their refusal is final, defining a hard line that must not be crossed even for urgent releases.
